meaning: Given this is the second verse for the remix, this is also the first verse in the original.
Rather than sing using his tenor voice, Breezy gives a surprisingly stellar (not to mention extremely vulgar) rap verse.
Possibly a nod to the 2 Chainz' verse in Mercy by Kanye

line: Baby, I’m a gangster, gentleman in disguise
vault_lines: Baby, I'm a gangster, gentleman in disguise
meaning:
Pop Smoke has used similar lines previously in his music, including “Hawk Em”:

I’m a gentlemen and gangster
Double G

In his XXL interview, Pop Smoke further elaborated on this:

I’m a gentleman. People think I’m just all gangster. I’m a double G homie: a gangsta and a gentleman. I’ve got sisters, you feel me. My sisters is like so sweet, calm and cool. You’ve got to be mindful that they’re females. They put me on like, ‘No Pop, you have to talk nice.’ So instead of saying, ‘What’s up! What’s good?!’ I say, ‘What’s the matter? What’s going on? Are you okay?’
Pop Smoke is referring to the 5167A Patek That says Patek Philippe on it

line: Tell me when to go, baby, when we gon’ slide? Baby, when we gon’ slide? Hey, uh Up all night, baby, when we gon’ slide? Yeah Up all night, baby, when we gon’ slide? Oh, oh Up all night, baby, when we gon’ slide?
meaning:
In a November 2019 Genius interview, H.E.R. revealed:


The Hyphy Movement. E-40, obviously, inspired that line. “Tell me when to go. Tell me when to go.” It’s direct. Like Kendrick said, E-40 head is thinking rational. So, that’s inspiration. Vallejo.

People in the Bay always say, “I’m finna slide. I’m finna slide,” or, “I’m going to come scoop.” That’s just the lingo, you know? So, when we going to slide? When we going? Where are we going? What are we doing? It’s just, like I said, that urgency of let’s be in this moment. What are we doing? Tell me what it is, you know? Tell me to go. I don’t even remember if the word came with the melody, but everything was just a flow. Like it felt so seamless in creation.

line: Ooh, I got five, you know it’s all live
vault_lines: Ooh, I got five, you know it's all live
meaning:
In a November 2019 Genius interview, H.E.R. revealed:

When I was a kid, I ain’t know what the song was talking about. I don’t think anybody as a kid knew what the song was talking about. In the song it’s more so like I’m a put $5 on gas, on a gas tank, just put it that way.

line: And we up ‘til six in the mornin’ When the sun rise, we be on it
vault_lines: And we up 'til six in the mornin'
meaning:
In a November 2019 Genius interview, H.E.R. revealed:

My favorite time of day is sunrise and sunset. So that moment, it’s just a small moment. The song is about a moment and the sunrise is a very short period of time. You have just a few minutes to catch it. So that’s where that comes from, it’s just being in the moment.

line: With the top down screamin’, “Money ain’t a thing”
vault_lines: With the top down screamin', "Money ain't a thing"
meaning:
In a November 2019 Genius interview, H.E.R. revealed:

It’s really just that free feeling, like we don’t care about anything. We ain’t worried about nothing but this moment right here. That’s where that inspiration came from.

line: Doin’ our thing, movin’ too fast Candy paint with the windows all black
vault_lines: Doin' our thing, movin' too fast
meaning:
In a November 2019 Genius interview, H.E.R. revealed:

When I think about the Bay Area, I think about being home in downtown Vallejo and seeing all the candy-paint cars. That’s really where that came from. I grew up seeing people ghost-riding the whip and doing donuts in these amazing blue, purple, different colored cars. I never got a candy-painted ride, unfortunately. But my ride is matte black, which I think is more me, if a little bit more mysterious and cool.

line: I don’t plan on gettin’ no sleep, while we
vault_lines: I don't plan on gettin' no sleep, while we
meaning:
In a November 2019 Genius interview, H.E.R. revealed:

With all my songs, I like it to be conversational. Most of my songs, it kind of sounds like a text message or something. So I felt like the whole song just needs to be a conversation between me and this person. Why we doing this? What’s it going to be?

line: Only keep the fam around me So let me know what it’s gon’ be
vault_lines: Only keep the fam around me
meaning:
In a November 2019 Genius interview, H.E.R. revealed:

My circle is really small. I’ve always been that way since I was a kid. My circle is super tight. I only keep the people around me who I’m super close to, who I know got my back. I’m a cancer so I have a hard time letting people in, so that’s really what it is. It’s like yo, you either all in or you not. You want to gas me and you want to be doing this and doing that, but if you ain’t about the real thing, then I’m sorry. That’s really what it is.

line: We on the same page, you the same way
vault_lines: We on the same page, you the same way
meaning:
In a November 2019 Genius interview, H.E.R. revealed:

Well for me, cause this is all personal for me, it was like we got to be on the same wavelength. Like we got to have the same kind of path, we got to be growing together and moving together. That’s really where it was coming from for me. I mean sometimes opposites attract in ways where we have to balance out each other, but it’s all about that climb together, that we’re doing together.

line: All he wanna do is gas me
vault_lines: All he wanna do is gas me
meaning:
In a November 2019 Genius interview, H.E.R. revealed:

You know when a guy’s trying to gas you up and make you feel good? That’s really what it is. I was so hyped when I realized it worked with YG’s intro because it was a flow. It didn’t even correlate, he just did it on his own. He said that on his own, so it worked out so perfectly.

However, in the remix to the original, YG’s intro was replaced by an intro and verse from Pop Smoke.
